newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Twelve injured in Colombian bomb blasts.
newsitem.headline: Twelve injured in Colombian bomb blasts.

text.p: Twelve people were injured on Tuesday in a total of three bomb blasts that rocked the northwest city of Medellin and Colombia's historic Caribbean port of Cartagena, authorities said.

Police said two of the blasts occurred simultaneously at dawn in a commercial area of Medellin, where 11 pedestrians were injured and windows were shattered for blocks around the site of the explosions.

One woman was injured in the blast in Cartagena in an explosion that broke the early-morning calm of the port that is one of Colombia's leading tourist attractions. As in Medellin, the Cartagena bomb went off in a commercial sector, police said.
Suspected leftist guerrillas detonated a bomb last Wednesday that killed five people and injured 40 others when it ripped through a Medellin office building.
Police said they had no immediate leads as to who was responsible for Tuesday's blasts.
